HxResult HxResFileAlert ( HxResFile_t *  pResFile,
uint32_t  id,
uint32_t *  pSelectedButton,
const char *  pLocale 
)

Show an alert from a .hxui file description.

This function shows an alert, using the icon, title, text, and buttons specified in an <alert> element of the resource file.

If you pass NULL for pSelectedButton, you're telling the API that you want the first button selected and that you don't care about what button was picked. This is often used with informational alerts that only have one button.

Parameters:
pResFile IN: a pointer to the resource file
id IN: the ID number of the <alert> object to read
pSelectedButton OUT: the button number used to dismiss the dialog or NULL.
pLocale IN: NULL means use default locale, otherwise process using specified locale string Unless you are using multiple locales within one HXUI file, you want to pass NULL here, as HxResFileOpen already picked the correct file for your locale based on the LANG environment variable and your setlocale() call.
Returns:
HxResult: Returns HX_OK if successful. Returns HX_MEMORY_ERROR if memory allocation fails. Can return other results from failure of individual HxUI calls. Returns HX_NOT_FOUND if no item was found that matched.

)

Show an alert from a .hxui file description.

This function shows an alert, using the icon, title, text, and buttons specified in an <alert> element of the resource file. The text of the alert, taken from the resource file, is treated as a printf-format string with the printf arguments passed at the end of the function.

If you pass NULL for pSelectedButton, you're telling the API that you want the first button selected and that you don't care about what button was picked. This is often used with informational alerts that only have one button.

Parameters:
pResFile IN: a pointer to the resource file
id IN: the ID number of the <alert> object to read
pSelectedButton OUT: the button number used to dismiss the dialog
pLocale IN: NULL means use default locale, otherwise process using specified locale string Unless you are using multiple locales within one HXUI file, you want to pass NULL here, as HxResFileOpen already picked the correct file for your locale based on the LANG environment variable and your setlocale() call.
Returns:
HxResult: Returns HX_OK if successful. Returns HX_MEMORY_ERROR if memory allocation fails. Can return other results from failure of individual HxUI calls. Returns HX_NOT_FOUND if no item was found that matched.

HxResult HxResFileClose ( HxResFile_t *  pResFile  ) 

Close a .hxui file.

This function closes an opened HxResFile_t handle. If the HxResFile_t was opened from a disk file, that is closed at this time. Any memory used by the HxResFile_t structure is also deallocated, but objects that were created from the resource file are still valid.

You are allowed to call this API before calling HxUiInit.

Parameters:
pResFile IN: a pointer to the resource file
Returns:
HxResult: Returns HX_OK if successful.

pData IN: pointer to arbitrary data, passed to callback function

HxResult HxResFileGetString ( HxResFile_t *  pResFile,
uint32_t  id,
char *  pBuffer,
int32_t *  pBytes,
const char *  pLocale 
)

Retrieve a string from a resource file.

This function returns the string with the given ID value that was specified by a <string> element in the resource file. This string is copied into a user-supplied buffer.

You are allowed to call this API before calling HxUiInit.

Parameters:
pResFile IN: a pointer to the resource file
id IN: the ID number of the <string> element
pBuffer IN: Buffer to receive the string, or NULL
pBytes IN/OUT: Pointer to the size of the character buffer. If buffer is too small returns the required minimum buffer size (including terminator).
pLocale IN: NULL means use default locale, otherwise process using specified locale string Unless you are using multiple locales within one HXUI file, you want to pass NULL here, as HxResFileOpen already picked the correct file for your locale based on the LANG environment variable and your setlocale() call.
Returns:
HxResult: Returns HX_OK if successful. Returns HX_MEMORY_ERROR if memory allocation fails. Returns HX_NOT_FOUND if no item was found that matched. Returns HX_BUFFER_TOO_SMALL if buffer is not large enough for string.

HxResult HxResFileGetStringPtr ( HxResFile_t *  pResFile,
uint32_t  id,
const char **  hString,
const char *  pLocale 
)

Retrieve a string from a resource file.

This function returns the string with the given ID value that was specified by a <string> element in the resource file. Unlike HxResFileGetString, this one returns a read-only pointer that can be used directly instead of copying the string to a buffer. This string pointer will remain valid until the resource file from which it was loaded is closed.

You are allowed to call this API before calling HxUiInit.

Parameters:
pResFile IN: a pointer to the resource file
id IN: the ID number of the <string> element
hString OUT: pointer to a const pointer to the string
pLocale IN: NULL means use default locale, otherwise process using specified locale string Unless you are using multiple locales within one HXUI file, you want to pass NULL here, as HxResFileOpen already picked the correct file for your locale based on the LANG environment variable and your setlocale() call.
Returns:
HxResult: Returns HX_OK if successful. Returns HX_NOT_FOUND if no item was found that matched.

HxResult HxResFileLoadContainer ( HxResFile_t *  pResFile,

HxContainer_t *  pContainer,
const char *  pLocale 
)

Load contents of .hxui container description into a container or window.

This function loads window objects into an existing container widget from a top-level <container> element in the resource file.

You can also pass HxWindow_t and HxDialog_t pointers as the pContainer argument to the function. The code only uses this pointer as a HxWidget_t pointer internally and makes it the parent of all the added items.

Parameters:
pResFile IN: a pointer to the resource file
id IN: the ID number of the top-level <container> object to read
pContainer IN: pointer to container widget or window that will be parent to items.
pLocale IN: NULL means use default locale, otherwise process using specified locale string Unless you are using multiple locales within one HXUI file, you want to pass NULL here, as HxResFileOpen already picked the correct file for your locale based on the LANG environment variable and your setlocale() call.
Returns:
HxResult: Returns HX_OK if successful. Returns HX_MEMORY_ERROR if memory allocation fails. Can return other results from failure of individual HxUI calls. Returns HX_NOT_FOUND if no item was found that matched.

This function creates a new HxMenu_t handle populated with the menu items specified in a <menu> element of the resource file. This is usually used for loading popup menus to be shown using HxMenuShow, but you can also use the loaded menu as a submenu for an existing menu.

HxResult HxResFileOpen ( const char *  pFilename,
HxResFile_t **  hResFile 
)

Open a .hxui file.

This function opens a .hxui file to be used by the other HxResFile functions.

This function will search multiple folders based on the active LC_MESSAGES locale as set by a call to setlocale(). The search order starts with the full locale name, then strips off any character set value, then strips off the country code. For example, if your LANG environment variable was set to "es_ES.utf8" and you had called setlocale(LC_ALL, "") to set the locale based on the environment, and you passed in "/test/foo.hxui", it would first look in "/test/es_ES.utf8/foo.hxui", then "/test/es_ES/foo.hxui", then "/test/es/foo.hxui", and finally "/test/foo.hxui" before giving up.

The same resource file should not be opened more than once at a time in a single application. This can cause problems with reserving ID numbers and error messages output on stderr.

You are allowed to call this API before calling HxUiInit, but you should not try to create any UI objects using the resource file until the UI system has been initialized.

Parameters:
pFilename IN: name of the .hxui file, relative to the current directory. This file is opened with read-only permissions.
hResFile OUT: a handle to the resource file
Returns:
HxResult: Returns HX_OK if successful. Returns HX_MEMORY_ERROR if memory allocation fails. Returns HX_MISSING_FILE if the filename is invalid. Returns HX_FAILURE for other failures.

HxResult HxResFileOpenBuffer ( const char *  pBuffer,
const char *  pDirectory,
HxResFile_t **  hResFile 
)

Open a .hxui file that is already in memory as a buffer.

This function treats a NULL-terminated in-memory buffer as a .hxui file. This lets you parse .hxui data that is embedded in a program or read from a non-file source. The buffer must remain valid until the HxResFile_t object is closed.

You are allowed to call this API before calling HxUiInit, but you should not try to create any UI objects using the resource file until the UI system has been initialized.

Parameters:
pBuffer IN: pointer to NULL-terminated character buffer holding the .hxui file contents to parse.
pDirectory IN: pointer to pathname to use as root directory for any file references seen in the .hxui buffer. If NULL, use current directory.
hResFile OUT: a handle to the resource file
Returns:
HxResult: Returns HX_OK if successful. Returns HX_MEMORY_ERROR if memory allocation fails. Returns HX_FAILURE for other failures.
